privacy.why: Eight people share one Claude account. These keep this machine's work off the shared account without changing anything for anyone else — they are user-scope, so they travel with the person, not the team.

house_style.font: Thmanyah only, everywhere (owner, 18 Sept 2026; widened 27 Sept 2026): the Thmanyah families (serif display, serif text, sans) are the only typefaces, in every project, deliverable and export, and in the public-store QA Wrap extension (licence risk raised once; the owner decided).
house_style.font_banned: Cairo — never proposed, never a fallback, in any project (owner, 2026-09-18)
house_style.font_source: The kit ships NO font files. Optional: set NJ_HOUSE_FONT_SOURCE (export.py) or NJ_HOUSE_FONT_DIR (install.py) to a folder of Thmanyah cuts you are licensed to use; install.py then installs them per-user so every renderer finds them by family name ('thmanyah serif display' / 'thmanyah serif text' / 'thmanyah sans'). Get the family from the publisher under its own licence (font.thmanyah.com).
house_style.pdf_extractor: poppler (pdftotext) — never pymupdf or pdfium for Arabic
house_style.documents: A4, Arabic/English bilingual, tagged PDFs, text must survive copy
house_style.why: Thamanya Serif replaced Cairo as the house face on 2026-09-18 and Cairo is banned. Historical note kept because it still explains an old fault: Cairo was once believed to corrupt Arabic on extraction; that was the audit tool, not the font — see pdf-typography. Entries below that still say Cairo (workflow_figure, PROJ) record how those deliverables were built before the switch.
house_style.arabic_pdf_guard: The stock anthropics/skills@pdf skill defaults to pypdf/pdfplumber, which lose Arabic words silently (0/9 and 6/9 vs poppler's 9/9). A guard note is patched into its SKILL.md locally and must be re-added after any re-fetch; CLAUDE.md carries the rule durably.

film.captions: Captions are the spoken words, verbatim, chunked, on screen while they are said. Separate card copy that paraphrases the voice reads as the caption talking about something else.
film.picture: The picture must show what the voice names at the moment it names it. A feature spoken over a different panel is a fault, not a stylistic choice.
film.voice: One TTS request per line — never split a line into fragments with different DSP flags and splice them (still true, still forbidden). For voice.py's Gemini-TTS engine, expressiveness is carried by the WRITING and a per-line natural-language DIRECTION string the model actually reads — see nj-writer/NARRATION.md §2 'Reconciling nj-kit's existing rule'. Flags still take '=': --rate=-6%, never --rate -6%. (Narration rule moved to NARRATION.md, 2026-09-21; this line is the pointer, kept for history.)
film.masters: Normalise every master to -14 LUFS integrated and -1 dBTP. Verify with ffmpeg ebur128, and with silencedetect for gaps.
film.no_warnings_in_frame: No product warnings in frame — grant notes, storage notes, amber cards. Only the story's deliberate failure may look like an error.
film.tutorials: Tutorials live on their own page, never stacked inside settings.
film.why: Every line is a rejection the owner made after a full render, and a render costs an hour of workers. Put them in the film bible's acceptance list and have the critic test each one before the director looks at frames.
film.no_unmasked_frame: The page-side mask script signals completion itself: its last act sets an invisible `data-PROJ-masked` attribute on <html> (re-set on every navigation as it re-applies). The recorder opens no capture window before waiting on that attribute (5 s timeout = loud step failure), stores maskReadyAt per step, and the composer starts each segment there, so the wait is never in the video and no pre-mask frame can be shown. A curtain is only a thin safety lifted by the same signal — never by fonts.ready or requestAnimationFrame, which blanked a whole recording on 2026-09-16. A frame scanner (raw-frame blankness, text-vs-dots in masked regions, blank composed frames, silent gaps) gates the build. The owner's design, 2026-09-16 12:15: cheaper and deterministic.
film.ffmpeg_zero_cut: Never pass a zero-length cut as `-t 0` to ffmpeg: on webm it decodes to EOF and silently pads 16–24 s of frozen picture into the video — this was the real source of the 'silent gaps' complaint (2026-09-16).
film.closing_still: Every tutorial video ends on a still of a finished request's status (masked, service name hidden), narrated; the document prints the same figure and never a table of end states or any mention of environment failures.
film.theme: dark mode only for QA Wrap films and presentations (owner, 2026-09-17: "the light version — dark mode is way better")

extension_testing.headed_one_at_a_time: Run the browser-extension suites headed, one suite at a time; the stress suite runs alone. Parallel headed runs fight over the profile and the window focus, and the failures they produce are not the product's.
extension_testing.classic_script_scope: Pages that load several classic (non-module) scripts share one global scope. A top-level const declared in two of them throws 'Identifier has already been declared' and the whole page dies. Scope helpers per file (IIFE) or declare once — unit tests do not catch it, only a behavioural page-render check does.
extension_testing.activetab_grant: A real activeTab grant IS obtainable under Playwright: dispatch the manifest's own keyboard shortcut through CDP Input.dispatchKeyEvent, which fires chrome.commands.onCommand. Dead routes, all measured: action.openPopup, the CDP Extensions domain, chrome.test, and both --auto-select-* flags.
extension_testing.why: Three weeks of harness time went into these three lines; each one was first diagnosed as a product bug.

workflow_figure.one_sheet: The SRS workflow figure is ALWAYS one A4 landscape sheet. Type size, band count and the gap between stages trade against each other, so they are searched together and scored on the printed point size — never settled one at a time, and never scaled down after the fact. A figure that cannot fit is split or the sheet grows; shrinking type is how a diagram ends up saying less than the paragraph beside it.
workflow_figure.font_family: Cairo only, and the font-family list ENDS at `sans-serif`. A named system fallback (Segoe UI) turns a missing glyph into a silently embedded system font instead of a visible failure. Captions may therefore use only glyphs Cairo has: it has no «←»/«→», so write «إلى» — the arrowhead already carries the direction.
workflow_figure.font_loading: Load the faces with `<link>`, never `@import` inside `page.setContent()` — `@import` never fetches there, so every measurement was silently taken in a fallback face and reported clean for weeks. Assert `document.fonts.check()` before measuring anything.
workflow_figure.metrics: Cairo advance width is not a per-character average: «رفض» runs 0.62 of the type size per character and «تعبئة نموذج الطلب (4 أقسام)» runs 0.34. Use the upper-bound model `size*(0.42*len+1.2)` — over-reserving costs air, under-reserving costs a collision. An Arabic line's glyph box is 1.82x the type size, not the line spacing.
workflow_figure.shapes: Stages are rounded rectangles; questions are diamonds, and only if the label actually asks one; a start and every ending is a STADIUM (rx = h/2) at the heaviest outline on the sheet, carrying a ✓ / ✕ / head — ISO 5807 gives the terminator a symbol of its own, and drawing it as a rectangle in a different colour rests the whole «did it finish or was it stopped» question on a pale green against a pale red. A decision's answer rides beside its own line with a white casing, never on top of another. A return is its own lane and never shares a corridor.
workflow_figure.why: Every line is a shipped fault, not a preference: a figure scaled down until it said less than its own caption; a PDF audit reporting SegoeUI embedded on the figure page only; weeks of 'clean' measurements taken in a fallback face because @import never fetched; captions drawn on top of each other because one average width under-reserved every short label. The full symptom-first catalogue is in workflow-diagram/SKILL.md — added 2026-09-06 along with the fit-by-search, measure-the-face and shape-vocabulary sections. Extended 2026-09-07 after a three-source audit of «طلب تسجيل منتج غذائي» measured the figure against the raw Flowable model and a fresh site walk: two of its endings existed nowhere but the figure, every desk read «مجموعة مرشحة» while the model assigns one of them round-robin to an individual, the service's hardest precondition («رقم كتاب تسجيل المنشأة» and its «تحقق») was in no source at all, and the first `--from 1` after the service was walked silently deleted half the model because `harvest()` chose one evidence file over the other. The new rules — walk as evidence, no invented ends, subtitles from the assignment, verify gates, the timer as an element, the caption dictionary and the two gates `caption-check.mjs` and the walk half of `flow-fidelity.mjs` — are all in workflow-diagram/SKILL.md. Extended again 2026-09-08 by a visual-design pass researched from primary sources: the palette was replaced (it measured CIEDE2000 0.35 apart under a protanopia simulation — a third of a just-noticeable difference), connectors gained three semantic classes crossed with a walked/unwalked channel, terminators became stadiums with glyphs, human and system tasks gained BPMN's own task-type markers, captions gained a halo, and the applicant's steps gained a common-region band. All of it is in workflow-diagram/SKILL.md § «Design rules», rule by rule with its source.
workflow_figure.evidence: A figure is drawn from a **site walk** first, the process model second, a template last, and each element carries which. Union the walk and the model — never choose between their files — let the walk's caption win verbatim, and draw a model element no walk reached with a lighter dashed outline and its own legend row. One caption dictionary maps each model flow name to the button's own wording, and a gate fails any other form. A verify widget with no `formcontrolname` is a field with a synthetic name; a boundary timer is its own shape; a desk's subtitle is its assignment, not its lane.
workflow_figure.design: 2026-09-08. The figure's design language is researched, not remembered, and every rule in workflow-diagram/SKILL.md § «Design rules» carries its source (ISO 5807, BPMN Method & Style, Camunda, WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.1/1.4.3/1.4.11, Okabe-Ito, Paul Tol SRON/EPS/TN/09-002, Palettailor, ISO 128-2, Imhof, NN/g on common region, W3C alreq). Four rules bind everything drawn: (1) colour is NEVER the only channel — a terminator is a stadium with a ✓ or a ✕, a system step carries a cog and a human task a head, and every class of line differs in weight AND dash AND colour; (2) contrast is computed, never eyeballed — title ink ≥ 7:1 on its own fill, outline ≥ 4.5:1 on it and ≥ 3:1 on paper; (3) role fills are anchored on Tol's `light` scheme because pale tints carry no category at all for a colour-blind reader — the reference chart's measured CIEDE2000 0.35 under a protanopia simulation, against 7.12 now; (4) three line weights, no more, thick-to-thin exactly 2:1, arrowheads left in SVG's default `strokeWidth` marker units so each head is proportional to its own line. Whether a path has been WALKED is a second channel crossed with the three classes — the class's own hue at a pale that still holds 3:1, thin, fine dash — never a fourth class, or a service whose refusals are all undemonstrated loses its refusals to grey.
workflow_figure.grouping: Who does a step is the colour of its box; WHERE THE PORTAL STOPS AND THE INSTITUTION STARTS is a boundary, and a boundary is drawn — a run of two or more consecutive applicant columns stands in a tinted band, one per grid row. Common region (Palmer, via NN/g) outranks proximity and similarity, and it is the only grouping cue available on a sheet whose columns are shared by every grid row and whose whitespace is already spent.
workflow_figure.key: The key registers from the drawing — a role only if a box is painted in it, a line class only if an edge is drawn in it — and shows each line class as A PIECE OF THE LINE, at its own weight, dash and head, with each role chip carrying that role's own badge. Colour chips cannot say «dashed, and lighter». The key is furniture that GROWS: whatever measures how many rows it takes must count the line rows too, or it under-measures and the key runs off the sheet. tools/srs/legend-sample.ts draws the whole thing on its own page from a synthetic flow, so the specimen cannot drift from what a real chart prints.

delegation.rule: NJ Governance v4 (2026-10-16): the Lead (Opus) briefs Sonnet leads (~/.claude/agents/sonnet-lead.md), a Sonnet lead briefs Haiku helpers (haiku-helper.md) in one foreground batch when the brief declares ITEMS=n (HELPERS_REQUIRED = 0 if n<6 else min(4, ceil(n/6))); helpers never spawn, depth max 2, up to 20 concurrent. Agents sleep until triggered and report once (receipt + <=25 lines). Hooks enforce it: nj_spawn.py logs every spawn (parent, child, depth), nj_guard.py denies remote pushes and merges to subagents and secrets reads to helpers. Gates: relay.py slots claim/release, relay.py verify over spawn logs, check_governance.py, tests test_v3/test_v4. Canonical: nj-delegate SKILL.md section 0 (v4). Tier policy unchanged: DETERMINISTIC / FREE-LOCAL / ECONOMY / STANDARD / FRONTIER, cheapest reliable first.

model_choice.note: Tier names are the policy; which runtime serves a tier is workspace mapping, kept out of the policy in nj-delegate/reference/runtime-map.md (2026-09-16).
model_choice.DETERMINISTIC: No model - scripts, CLI, tests, parsers, static analysis, checksums, focused greps/counts, diff/stat, schema checks, duplicate detection, log preprocessing, failed-test extraction, mechanical validation.
model_choice.FREE-LOCAL: Only classes a local/free runtime has demonstrably handled reliably here; never a first trial on delivery-critical work. No such runtime is installed on this machine.
model_choice.ECONOMY: Extraction, summarisation, discovery, bounded routine reasoning, low-risk test generation, listings, renames, copies, exports, mechanical checklist updates.
model_choice.STANDARD: Implementation to a spec, debugging, focused investigation, normal review and scoring, authoring from a model or a spec (Arabic included).
model_choice.FRONTIER: Ambiguity, architecture, hard root cause, security, production- or data-sensitive change, complex orchestration, high-risk adjudication. Never chosen for importance, client visibility, language or the fact that code is edited; no per-batch ceiling since 2026-09-17; the brief names the reasoning capability required.

delegation.graphify_first: The repo graph lives at <project-root>/graphify-out/ (built 2026-09-06 over PROJ-tests code, the 15 old SRS docx, templates, PDFs). Answer 'where is X / what calls Y / which service has Z' with `graphify query` before grepping; rebuild with `/graphify . --update` after large changes.
delegation.agent_prompts: An agent starts with none of the conversation, so the prompt carries the absolute paths, the exact commands, the constraints and the standing rules that would otherwise be broken silently — staging only, deletions to the recycle bin, do not touch the videos, PYTHONUTF8=1 — and it must demand a COMPLETE FACTUAL REPORT, because the director relays that report and never re-derives it. The director relays failures and skipped items faithfully and does the review itself.
delegation.why: Measured worker explosions and rebuild loops dominated cost, so the policy minimises total compute rather than director tokens alone: deterministic work and existing evidence first, minimum-sufficient delegation, and the strongest tier reserved for actual judgement. 2026-09-16 (the owner: lowest-cost tier that is good enough + effort) the policy was made vendor-neutral - five capability tiers, no provider or model names in the core policy, the tier->runtime map moved to an on-demand reference - and tool-call budgeting was replaced by token/context control, because the 2026-09-16 evidence showed workers under the call cap running 2-3x over budget on wide reads, three authorings at ~180k, a bulk copy at 6.7x, and an always-on interpreter costing ~45k tokens x ~30 messages a day. Routing evidence: on 2026-09-15, 14 of 22 FRONTIER runs (61 percent of FRONTIER spend, 28 percent of the whole day, estimated tokens) were scoring, verification, authoring or apply-a-known-rule stages a cheaper tier would have done at the same rework and partial rates. Classify by the reasoning the stage requires; two downgrades (a review that is mostly scoring is STANDARD and FRONTIER reads only the disputed cells; authoring from a model or a spec is STANDARD even in Arabic); two upgrades (failed twice for the same cause - escalate the cause as its own short run, not the task; client output with no gate - and writing the gate is cheaper than raising the tier), never an upgrade for an environment failure; every brief names an EFFORT level set by the stage, not the tier. Evidence: PROJ/PROJ-tests/artifacts/ops/model-routing-audit-2026-09-16.md and fable-usage-rca-2026-09-08.md.
delegation.set: NJ Governance v4, live 2026-10-16; nj-delegate section 0 is the one canonical statement.
delegation.modes: nj-delegate is the single source of truth for worker count: minimum-sufficient for the critical path, set per batch by FIT - Lead context headroom, machine/rate capacity, and the quality the stage needs (owner, 2026-09-16 18:55) - never by a fixed quota. Measured capacity facts on this machine (two concurrent recorders; five open-ended FRONTIER loops exhaust the 5-hour window in ~50 min) are inputs to that judgement, not caps. Eco = the user's ceiling of one; Max = the user's named N. Zero stays valid in every mode.

agent_ops.rule: nj-agent-ops is optional script mode. It inherits the nj-delegate count rule (no cap of its own), relays worker results through <project>/.agent-ops/results/<run-id>/, batches feedback, carries the per-run measurement schema (runtime, tier, task class, role, cached/uncached input, output, reasoning tokens, model calls, tool calls, workers, retries, duration, separate execution/verification/final status, defects, escalations, cost with an actual-or-estimated basis), and keeps one ECONOMY interpreter per session, spawned only on a trigger (long message, mixed Arabic/English, or a change to a running brief; the owner 2026-09-29; standing 09-18 -> 09-29, conditional 09-16 -> 09-18 are history), never polled, and writes one calibration row per task with `relay.py batch`. Since 2026-09-16 19:40 (the owner) the error/attempt cap is budget and progress, not a count: a worker continues while its budget is under 80 %, each attempt is a different cause-classified fix and the evidence moved; it stops with QUESTION when evidence repeats; two questions then skip. Since 2026-09-16 20:15 (the owner) the director manages only (no probes/edits/gates itself) and workers report once at the end, stopping early only for a QUESTION.
agent_ops.why: File relay and batch feedback reduce context and API churn. The interpreter was permanent per user message (owner, 2026-09-15); measurement on 2026-09-16 put it at ~45k tokens per message over ~30 messages a day, much of it restating short unambiguous English, so it was made CONDITIONAL rather than removed - the mechanism has proven value on mixed-language, long, informal or ambiguous messages, and the same test now applies to any other standing per-stage helper call. Section 3 of nj-agent-ops carries nj-delegate section 3 verbatim: the director runs the classify/downgrade/upgrade/effort procedure per stage and pastes the budget line (Tier: X because <reasoning type>; effort: Y; budget: uncached input <= N, output <= M, model calls <= K, files read <= F; tool_calls <= T runaway cap only) into every brief; after each batch any run over 1.5x its class budget gets a one-line CAUSE note in the ledger and the next same-class brief is tightened.

delegation.budgets: Budgets are tokens and context, never tool calls (revised 2026-09-16: workers stayed under the call cap and still ran 2-3x over budget on wide reads). Every brief carries: uncached input, output, model calls, files/context read; tool_calls is a runaway cap only. Derived class budgets (from 2026-09-15 medians, estimated not counter-measured): FRONTIER 150k uncached input / 25 files, STANDARD 65k / 15, ECONOMY 12k / 8. Where a counter is unavailable a labelled proxy may be used and is never reported as a measurement. An overrun never auto-terminates valuable work: stop, name the cause (context too wide / duplicate reads / environment rework / capability) and fix that cause - only 'capability' justifies a higher tier, in writing. Context economy is a standing rule for every mode: targeted search, symbols, exact line ranges, diff hunks, failed tests only, unique error signatures; no full-file read when a section suffices, no broad repo read by default, no two workers rediscovering the same structure, evidence extracted once and reused by path.
delegation.retry: Cause-based retry: classify every failure (CAPABILITY_LIMIT / CONTEXT_DEFECT / IMPLEMENTATION_DEFECT / TOOL_FAILURE / ENVIRONMENT_FAILURE / TEST_FAILURE / AMBIGUOUS_REQUIREMENT / AUTHORIZATION_BLOCKER) and fix that cause. Never the same prompt again, never an automatic tier escalation (only CAPABILITY_LIMIT, in writing), never another worker because the first failed. Attempt cap is budget and progress, not a count (2026-09-16 19:40): continue while under 80 % budget, each attempt a different fix, evidence moved; else QUESTION n/2; two questions per batch, then skip and mark.
delegation.reporting: A worker report is a receipt of at most 25 lines on six headings - STATUS / FINDING / EVIDENCE / FILES-SYMBOLS / RISK / NEXT ACTION - plus a CHANGED list from git status, and the stage detail file (named in the brief's RESUME line) holds everything else (owner, 2026-09-29, D2: one rule in every file). No raw logs or full files in the receipt. The old hard 150-word cap was dropped on 2026-09-16 because it truncated findings; the 25-line receipt works because the detail file carries the rest.
delegation.high_rework: Browser, recording and environment-sensitive workflows (2026-09-16: twelve recording attempts lost to four silently failing helpers): no auto-upgrade of tier, deterministic preprocessing, input and environment validation before any model work, preparation separated from reasoning, successful intermediate artefacts preserved, retry from the failure point when safe, successful steps never repeated, rework rate measured independently. Procedure on demand in nj-delegate/reference/high-rework.md.
delegation.experiments: An optimisation is proved against a baseline of the same task class in the ledger, and accepted only if it reduces cost, context, frontier attention, duplicate work or model calls without materially reducing correctness, testing, review, evidence or safety. Total input tokens alone is not the metric; estimated figures are labelled estimated and never mixed with actual.

session_lessons_2026_09_17.rule: A worker never ends its turn while its own background work (a recorder, a monitor) is still running - foreground waits only. Every worker launch gets a ledger row, no exceptions. The director reads `date` before quoting a deadline, never relays a generalisation without its count, never sweeps without one positive sample, and asks once (not twice, not by guessing) when a new instruction contradicts the last one on the same point. A recurring fault class becomes a one-file registry entry, not a repeated patch to shared code; shared pipeline code has one owner at a time and is checked against a stored baseline before it ships.
session_lessons_2026_09_17.why: One 22h PROJ user-manual session (PROJ-tests/artifacts/ops/session-review-2026-09-17.md) measured 96 redeliveries against 16 deliveries, one shared file patched 9 times in a day, a ~12-wake director storm in 3 minutes from agents ending turns on background monitors, and ~1M tokens spent interpreting messages under ten words. None of it was a reasoning failure - the review's own conclusion is 'not recommended: more workers, a stronger model, looser gates.' It was unwritten director discipline and mask/staging logic living in ad hoc patches instead of a registry. Full numbers and the fix plan (P1-P8, W1/W2/W3) are in the session review; the rules above are what generalises past this one project.

delegation.director: Runtime mapping is a workspace fact, not policy: see nj-delegate/reference/runtime-map.md (Lead and tier->runtime table, chosen at the top of a session and never switched mid-session).
delegation.dispatch: the owner, 2026-09-29 (D3): a worker that builds or edits runs in the FOREGROUND, so he can watch it and his messages cannot kill or derail it mid-phase; read-only research and reading may run in the background. Every brief carries a FOCUS line either way: a mid-run message that does not start AMEND: is not a task (worker-rules R10). Why: in UI round 2 an owner 'progress?' message derailed a background stage into answering and returning with no files, and another killed a running tool call silently.
delegation.brief_fields_2026_09_29: The brief template and check_governance.py REQUIRED_BRIEF_FIELDS gained FOCUS, ENTRY_SMOKE (one check through the real caller or entry point, R14), RESUME (the stage detail file / progress log a resumed run continues from) and a gated CHANGED line in RECEIPT; worker-rules gained R13-R17 (leave nothing running, test through the real caller, a green gate proves it looked, numbers computed never typed, every claim points at a tool result). Each was paid for in QA Wrap UI round 2 (prompt audit work/prompt-audit-0929).

PROJ.headed: PROJ_HEADED=1 on every portal, harvest, recorder and smoke run — always, on this project. The tools already launch `headless: false`; without the flag they add `--window-position=-3000,-3000` and the window is parked off-screen. The flag is not "make it headed", it is "let me watch it", and the client asked to watch.
PROJ.git_bash: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 on any command whose argument is a portal route — anything starting with `/` — or Git Bash rewrites /equipment/services/… into a Windows path before the tool ever sees it.
PROJ.target: ${PORTAL_URL} only. Staging is the deployment, not a sandbox: filing costs a real request, a fee and a queue wait, and a wrong staff-side press costs the request itself with nothing to undo it. Never point a run at production.
PROJ.deliverable_names: Every deliverable states its kind in its own Arabic name, so a folder of them reads without opening anything: «<الاسم> - SRS», «<الاسم> - دليل المستخدم», «<الاسم> - دليل الموظف». Every file inside repeats the folder's name, because a PDF is mailed and filed away from its folder. Names are short on purpose — MAX_PATH is 260 and a full cover title carried by both a folder and a filename reached 231. Identity stays English: the flow id is the argument, the key and the checkpoint name; only what a reader opens is Arabic.
PROJ.pdf: Cairo, one family for every document this project prints, declared once in `.pdf-typography.json` at the repo root with no per-document override. The house face, not a per-document choice.

video_transcription.rule: Transcribe a video from its own frames, never from a scrape of the page it sits on. Measured 2026-09-07 on an Instagram reel: a web fetch returned 17 of 20 on-screen items, in the wrong order, with the source's own red x marks silently dropped - which inverted the meaning of three of them - and reported one item as unreadable. A 3x lanczos crop of the same region made all twenty legible. A pre-transcribed list is a draft, not a source.
video_transcription.tools: yt-dlp --dump-json for provenance and yt-dlp -f best for the file; no login needed for a public reel and none is used. ffmpeg select='gt(scene,N)' to find out whether there are any cuts at all - a talking-head reel returns zero at both 0.2 and 0.05, which is the signal that the final frame accumulates the whole list. Then fps=1 and fps=4 stills.
video_transcription.timing: Time an item's appearance by masked difference against the FINAL frame, not by argmax of the frame-to-frame difference. The mask is the caption glyphs themselves (near-white cores plus black outlines); the first sample where the difference collapses is the landing moment, and the result must come out monotonic across all items - that monotonicity is the check that the row geometry was right. argmax fails wherever the speaker's head or hand crosses the row band: it put two items 3 and 7 seconds early on the measured reel.
video_transcription.audio: Local speech-to-text is available since 2026-10-01: faster-whisper (small, CPU int8) via `uv run --with faster-whisper --with "av>=15,<16" python tr.py in.wav out.txt` (av pin: unpinned resolves to 19 and crashes; av<15 has no Windows wheel). The audio is still never sent anywhere - not to Groq/OpenAI, not through agent-reach transcribe. Where a reel burns in word-by-word captions, sample that strip at each item's landing time and montage it - it corroborates the list and disambiguates abbreviations. See house_style.social_media.
video_transcription.cleanup: The download and every frame are recycled with safe-delete when the transcript is written. Nothing is uploaded, and the transcript file - not the video - is the checkpoint the next stage reads.

The gate fails on horizontal overflow, elements past the viewport, a declared font that did not load, Arabic set in a face with no Arabic coverage, contrast below WCAG AA, and colours outside the tokens. Origin: Instagram reel DchdDmDj37s (noobs prompt / pros hand over a design system / legends give the agent eyes), 2026-09-17. Three gate bugs were found and fixed on first use and are worth not repeating: document.fonts.check defaults to weight 400 (a page loading only 500/700 reads as missing), contrast over a gradient is not computable from one colour (guessing white fails every dark panel), and webfonts need document.fonts.ready rather than a sleep.
house_style.skill_descriptions: <=40 words per skill description, standing rule since the 2026-09-18 audit. Descriptions are the ONLY always-on token cost - loaded in every session before any work - so they are the one place where trimming pays every time. A description's job is ROUTING, so every distinctive trigger phrase stays and only the prose around it goes. Over-trimming does not save tokens, it stops the skill from ever being found, which is the expensive failure.
house_style.arabic_triggers_protected: Every Arabic trigger phrase is protected in any description trim: تدقيق, مراجعة لغوية, «تدقيق الوثيقة», «راجع الوثيقة», «هل الوثيقة مطابقة», «مخطط سير العمل», «إجراء», «شكل التصميم», «التصميم مش مظبوط», نظف الصوت, معالجة الصوت, موسيقى خلفية, «دليل المستخدم», «دليل الموظف». house_style.third_party_skills: A third-party skill is KEPT OR REMOVED, NEVER REWRITTEN IN PLACE. install.py re-fetches it from its upstream repo, so an in-place edit is either overwritten on the next machine or freezes a fork that stops getting upstream fixes. One exception, and it is data rather than an edit: the description, re-applied from description-overrides.json by scripts/apply-descriptions.py. A third-party skill that is 80% out of scope is removed, and the 20% worth keeping is folded into one of ours as a short section. Verdict SAFE. It is here because 'refactor this' had no house answer and the alternative was improvising one per session. What it actually supplies: the five-phase safe process (prepare with tests in place -> identify one smell -> change small, test, commit -> verify behaviour and performance -> clean up), ten named smells with before/after diffs, and a seventeen-row table of Fowler operations to name a move with instead of describing it. TWO THINGS TO KNOW BEFORE FOLLOWING IT. (1) Its examples are TypeScript and class-shaped - interfaces, abstract Validator chains, builder patterns. Take the operations, not the idioms; on QA Wrap's classic-JS MV3 extension the Strategy and Chain-of-Responsibility sections are wrong tools, and its 'introduce type safety' section does not apply at all. (2) Its 'When NOT to refactor' list is the load-bearing half and is the easiest part to skim past - code that works and will not change again, critical code without tests, and 'just because' are all rejections. Applied honestly it deletes most of a refactor backlog before any editing starts, which is the point. THE HOUSE ADDITION IT DOES NOT KNOW, and which cost real time on QA Wrap 2026-09-07: an MV3 extension has constraints the skill never mentions, and every one of them turns a textbook-correct extraction into a shipped bug. The service worker's boot graph has a hard byte budget (800 KB, enforced by extension/tools/test-worker-imports.mjs), so splitting one big file into modules can FAIL the build by adding graph weight even though no logic changed. MV3 forbids dynamic import() in a worker, so lazy-loading is not the escape hatch it is everywhere else. And chrome.runtime message names and chrome.storage keys are a wire protocol shared with content scripts, the popup, the side panel and the options page - 'Rename Method/Variable' from the skill's own table is FORBIDDEN on those, because the rename is silent and the other end fails at runtime, not at test time. Classic scripts on one page also share a global scope, so a top-level const moved into a second file that the same page loads throws 'Identifier has already been declared' and kills the page - unit tests never see it. Rule of thumb that came out of it: extract WITHIN a file before extracting ACROSS files, and make every move carry a unit test that would have caught its own regression.

items.claude-security@claude-plugins-official: Anthropic's own in-session vulnerability scanner. Installed to user scope 2026-09-07 with `claude plugin marketplace add anthropics/claude-plugins-official` then `claude plugin install claude-security@claude-plugins-official`. WHY: (1) the owner asked for it by name. (2) It was reviewed as PASS on 2026-09-07 (SECURITY-REVIEW-2026-09-06.md, the claude-security addendum): zero network egress anywhere in the package, git invoked through argument lists and never a shell string, no credential paths read, no eval/exec, no obfuscation, `disable-model-invocation: true` so it runs only when a person names it. (3) The one thing that made it the owner's call rather than a worker's is the hooks - three of them, a banner on UserPromptExpansion and a metrics counter on Bash PostToolUse/PostToolUseFailure, narrowed by an `if` to its own scripts - and they run hooks.py, whose imports are stdlib only and which sends nothing anywhere. Stdlib-only, no egress, and still session-wide: that is why it waited for a word. WHAT WAS NOT DONE: its SKILL.md nudges the model to recommend auto permission mode once per job. That nudge was not acted on. No permission mode was changed, and the only settings.json keys the install touched are `extraKnownMarketplaces` and `enabledPlugins`. It does not replace nj-security-review (which asks whether somebody else's skill will act against you) or the built-in /security-review (which asks about the pending diff); this one asks where the vulnerabilities are in a whole repository. Listed in KNOWN_SOURCES so a new machine re-fetches it.

governance_v4.why: v4 turns the trigger-only hierarchy (the owner 2026-10-14) into enforced tooling: typed agents, spawn/guard hooks, and runtime limits. A new machine needs all of it or v4 is prose only. export.py bundles agents and hooks; install.py copies them (backup, idempotent) and merges env.

agents.why: defines the Sonnet service lead the Lead delegates every build/fix to: owns one phase, single writer, briefs haiku-helpers, commits only, reports once.
defines the Haiku helper for mechanical bounded work: no Agent tool so it cannot spawn, cannot push or merge, no secrets reads, reports once.

hooks.why: logs every subagent spawn with parent, child type, model and depth to ~/.claude/logs/spawn-log.jsonl and <project>/.agent-ops/spawns.jsonl, because hook input carries no parent/depth; relay.py verify audits depth and hierarchy from it.
PreToolUse guard that makes two v4 rules mechanical: subagents may not push or merge (the Lead merges) and haiku helpers may not touch credential paths.
